description: This dataset supports intrusion detection for KNX building automation systems reached over IP networks through the KNXnet/IP protocol, which is often deployed without encryption or authentication. It was published on Zenodo on 27 August 2025 (version 1.0.0) by Christos Dalamagkas of the Public Power Corporation of Greece, Panagiotis Radoglou-Grammatikis and Pavlos Bouzinis of MetaMind Innovations, Thomas Lagkas of Democritus University of Thrace, Vasileios Argyriou of Kingston University and Panagiotis Sarigiannidis of the University of Western Macedonia, within the EU-funded AI4CYBER project. Eight attack scenarios were developed against a KNXnet/IP infrastructure and captured: property-read fuzzing, master reset, network and bus scanning, flooding with valid and fuzzed group value writes and reads, and unauthorised group value writes. Coverage: one test infrastructure. Access: eight ZIP files of about 8 to 215 MB and a README on Zenodo. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: attacks were run on a test infrastructure whose location is not stated in the metadata read. Simulation uses: training detectors and testing the cyber resilience of building controls such as lighting, HVAC and access. Related records: the Sharjah smart building IoT data.
